title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

Major indices remain in a mixed and fragile technical position. Three of the four major indices are trading below their 10-day and 20-day moving averages, with only MDY still holding above those short-term levels. QQQ remains the clear weak link after breaking below its 50-day moving average and undercutting major pivot lows on distributive action. Buyers need to step in soon and start repairing the damage; otherwise, sellers remain in control.

The sector picture remains highly selective. Financials, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Defensives continue to show the best combination of price action, trend strength, and relative strength. These remain the primary areas of focus. Energy is in pullback mode, still unable to breakout of its long base, while Consumer Cyclicals, and Industrials are emerging. Technology and Materials continue to lack the right blend of technical strength and relative strength, making them avoids for now.

Breadth and momentum remain flat, with new highs roughly equal to new lows. That reflects a lack of clear participation and conviction beneath the surface. Overall, this remains a mixed, volatile, and sloppy tape. Until participation broadens and leadership becomes more decisive, traders should maintain a less aggressive posture, stay highly selective, and focus only on stocks and sectors showing the strongest combination of relative strength, clean structure, and constructive price action.

Tactical Plan of Action

1) Trend & Market Structure

The major indices remain in a mixed and fragile technical state. Three of the four major indices are below their 10-day and 20-day moving averages, with only MDY still holding above those short-term levels. QQQ remains the clear weak link, having broken below its 50-day moving average and undercut major pivot lows on distributive action.

The market has not fully broken, but sellers currently have the upper hand. Buyers need to step in soon and begin repairing the technical damage. Until that happens, the tape should be treated with caution.

Tactical guidance

  • Maintain a defensive and selective posture.

  • Keep exposure around 30–45% of normal.

  • Avoid broad market exposure while most indices remain below their 10-day and 20-day moving averages.

  • Treat QQQ and Technology weakness as a major caution flag.

  • If buyers reclaim the 10/20-day moving averages and breadth improves, exposure can gradually increase.

  • If QQQ remains below the 50-day and other indices weaken further, reduce exposure quickly.

2) Breadth & Momentum

Breadth and momentum remain flat, with new highs roughly equal to new lows. That reflects a lack of clear participation, conviction, and directional force beneath the surface.

This is not a broad internal collapse, but it also does not provide enough support for aggressive long exposure. The market remains selective, choppy, and vulnerable to further downside if buyers fail to step in.

Tactical guidance

  • Use breadth as the risk throttle.

  • If new highs begin expanding and new lows contract, exposure can increase toward 45–55%.

  • If breadth remains flat, keep exposure capped around 30–45%.

  • If new lows begin to expand meaningfully, cut exposure to 20–30%.

  • Do not press the long side until participation improves.

3) Sector Focus & Rotation

The sector picture remains mixed but selective. Energy, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Financials continue to show the best combination of price action, trend strength, and relative strength. These are the only areas deserving meaningful focus for now.

Technology, Consumer Defensives, Consumer Cyclicals, Industrials, and Materials continue to lack the right combination of technical strength and relative strength. These groups should remain avoids until they repair.

Tactical guidance

  • Focus primarily on Energy, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Financials.

  • Prioritize stocks in these groups that are holding above key moving averages and showing strong relative strength.

  • Avoid Technology until QQQ reclaims the 50-day and rebuilds structure.

  • Avoid Consumer, Industrials, and Materials until relative strength and price action improve.

  • Do not force trades outside the leadership groups.

4) Stock Selection & Entries

This is not a broad breakout-buying environment. The best opportunities are likely to come from stocks in the few sectors showing real relative strength and clean structure. Everything else should be treated with skepticism.

Prioritize

  • Healthcare, Real Estate, and Financial names showing strong relative strength.

  • Stocks holding above rising 20-day and 50-day moving averages.

  • Tight bases near highs while the broader market weakens.

  • Constructive pullbacks with volume drying up.

  • Undercut-and-reclaim setups near logical support.

  • Stocks resisting market weakness while indices remain fragile.

Avoid

  • Technology names breaking support with QQQ below the 50-day.

  • Stocks below declining 10-day, 20-day, or 50-day moving averages.

  • Loose, wide, volatile patterns.

  • Breakouts in lagging sectors.

  • Dip buys in damaged charts.

  • Buying anything simply because it looks cheap.

5) Trade Management & Risk Controls

Capital preservation remains the priority. The tape is tradable in select areas, but the broader backdrop is still fragile. Position sizing should stay conservative, and failed trades should be cut quickly.

Risk controls

  • Use ¼ to ½ normal size on new entries.

  • Use ¾ size only for exceptional setups in the strongest groups.

  • Avoid full-size positions until indices reclaim short-term moving averages and breadth improves.

  • Cut failed breakouts quickly.

  • Take partial profits into quick strength.

  • Trail strong positions with the 10-day or 20-day moving average.

  • Do not average down into broken charts.

  • Raise cash from names losing the 50-day or undercutting key pivot lows.

6) Exposure Scenarios

Base Case: Fragile, Mixed Tape

Three of the four major indices are below their 10-day and 20-day moving averages, QQQ is below its 50-day, and breadth/momentum remain flat.

Exposure: 30–45%
Cash: 50–65%
Posture: Defensive, selective, capital-preservation focused

Selective Leadership Scenario

This develops if Energy, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Financials continue to lead while breadth remains stable.

Action: Maintain 35–50% exposure.

Add only to clean setups in the strongest groups.

Repair Scenario

This develops if QQQ reclaims the 50-day, the major indices regain their 10-day and 20-day moving averages, and new highs expand.

Action: Increase exposure toward 45–60%.

Focus on stocks reclaiming support with strong relative strength.

Continued Weakness Scenario

This develops if QQQ remains weak, other indices lose support, and new lows expand.

Action: Reduce exposure toward 20–30%.

Raise cash, cut weak positions, and avoid new long exposure.

Breakdown Scenario

This develops if SPY, MDY, and IWM lose their 50-day moving averages while QQQ continues lower.

Action: Reduce exposure toward 10–20%.

Move to capital preservation and wait for a new stabilization process.

Bottom Line

The market remains mixed, fragile, and sloppy. QQQ is clearly damaged, most major indices are below their 10-day and 20-day moving averages, and breadth/momentum remain flat. Buyers need to step in soon to repair the technical deterioration; otherwise, sellers remain in control.

The right posture is defensive but engaged. Focus only on Energy, Healthcare, Real Estate, and Financials, avoid weak groups, keep position sizes small, and preserve capital until participation broadens and the indices begin to reclaim key moving averages.
